data.narrative:
Space42, a public-listed Space & Aerospace company formed via merger of Bayanat and Yahsat, has raised $695M+ in ECA financing. The valuation universe comprises 13 peers: 5 public equities (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private entities including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ICEYE, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Standard triangulation methods prove inapplicable here. Peer-median analysis cannot proceed due to insufficient narrow-stage comparables within Space & Aerospace—while 14 same-sector peers exist globally, none satisfy simultaneous filters for stage alignment and valuation tier comparability, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring, though theoretically feasible given the sector trades at a 24.4x P/S median across the five public comps, cannot be executed absent the target's revenue figure, which remains undisclosed.

The analysis reaches an impasse. No quantitative valuation range can be defensibly derived from the available data. Progression would require either: disclosure of Space42's revenue and near-term earnings guidance to enable P/S or EV/EBITDA anchoring to public multiples; identification of sufficiently comparable private-stage financing rounds; or management-provided forward metrics. Until such inputs surface, a rigorous analytical conclusion remains unsupported.
